name: movie_etaori_lpqi_2orbits_gap_node90
label: Movie: eta Ori Aa, two 8-night orbits 323 days apart, line of nodes rotated by 90 deg (H-alpha, MPD)
notes: The movie_etaori_lpqi_orbit_node90 plan twice, with a 323-day break between the two eight-night runs: 323 / 7.98763 = 40.44 orbits, so the second run samples the orbit half a step (0.0625 in phase) away from the first -- the largest offset a whole-night gap can give, and the only way to sample other phases with P so close to 8 days. Both runs assume the full hour-angle window (323 days later the season is six weeks earlier, still within October-March).
The question is whether the offset phases break the fringe-alias islands that the consecutive 16-night plan leaves.
The eclipse nights, the third light and the per-night fit are as in the PA 0 campaign; compare the two movies' fringe amplitudes and the final sigma(a)/a.
